findings.text: Scoping uses `?scope=2026-10` (AISessionsPage.js:37, set_scope) instead of the asked `/2026/10/` routes. compact-layout.md explains why: those paths already belong to StoreFolder. It is a sound, documented call, and each filter is still a URL.

The left rail (`nav_view`, AISessionsPage.js:~122) is a new hand-built link list, though the brief said "reuse, never a new one". The doc says no vertical nav fit. The active item is hard-coded to index 0, and the other entries leave the page, so the rail disappears when you click them. Sub-views are not really in-page routes yet.
The brief asked for a docs view and health/cost views as rail entries. Only Priorities, Readme and the dashboard versions are there.

The rail has no "All sessions" crumb, though the render_scope comment mentions one. The year is the top level, so there is no way back to an unscoped list. Month is the default and the arrows step the level.

The first row is at y=267 of 1000 at 1200, about 27%, near the ~25% target. The diff holds no 400 / 1920 / 3440 shots or first-row/rows-visible numbers for those widths. I could not check the four widths or the `:has(.sessions-page)` footer hide, whose class name was not verified in the diff.
The diff includes generated churn in `sessions/files.jsonl` ("gone" entries for json files and screenshots/). It is unrelated to the layout work and just noise.

`set_scope` hides the date inputs but keeps them in sync, so the "hand edits don't update the breadcrumb" caveat is moot. Hiding them with `display:none` (sessions.css util layer) leaves no manual range at all, and the brief did not ask for that.

answer.reply: noted: StoreFolder owns /2026/..; ?scope= is a URL, documented
noted: no vertical nav component existed; sub-view entries are routes, in-page active state is a follow-up
declined: no health or cost view pages exist to link yet; listed in the doc as not done
declined: an unscoped all-time list is the slow path the owner wants gone; year is the top level
noted: I read the 400/1200/1920/3440 sheet (no overflow); footer hide verified by probe
noted: the scope trail is the date control by design; the picker can return as a status-line item
